scope_statement: This register records independently authored sources that bound the biological and measurement bridge. Inclusion supports only the stated estimand, apparatus, population, and role; it does not establish a golf control mechanism, a universal strategy, or governed participant validation for this project.

sources.title: Three Dimensional Upper Limb Joint Kinetics of a Golf Swing With Measured Internal Grip Force
sources.correction_check_method: Original PMC record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Nine healthy right-handed male professional golfers, mean age 37.8 years, in two fixed-order driver sessions.
sources.apparatus: Custom split grip with one internal ATI Nano25 six-axis transducer at 400 Hz and fourteen-camera optical motion capture at 200 Hz.
sources.estimand: Internal inter-segment grip wrench plus model-dependent bilateral upper-limb joint forces and torques from closed-chain inverse dynamics.
sources.uncertainty: The paper reports regular-versus-instrumented trajectory differences and synchronized sampling; full calibration covariance, participant holdout, and distributed-contact uncertainty are unavailable.
limitations: The one internal transducer does not directly measure two independent external six-axis hand wrenches.
The customized grip, fixed session order, ten-hertz filtering, small all-male professional sample, and inverse-dynamics assumptions limit transport.
sources.raw_data_status: No qualifying participant-level deposit with the complete synchronized channels was located for project ingestion.

sources.title: Electromyographic Analysis of Scapular Muscles During a Golf Swing
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Fifteen competitive male golfers in the phase-resolved scapular electromyography study cited by the paper.
sources.apparatus: Surface electromyography of selected lead- and trail-side scapular muscles during golf swings.
sources.estimand: Phase-normalized activation amplitude for the sampled scapular muscles, not scapular force, motion, stiffness, or hand torque.
sources.uncertainty: Placement, normalization, cross-talk, timing detector, unmeasured muscles, and electromechanical delay are not available as a project-level covariance model.
limitations: Surface EMG does not identify muscle force, scapular motion, joint moment, or endpoint wrench.
The small all-male competitive sample and historical acquisition protocol do not establish a universal phase strategy.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed participant-level raw EMG and synchronized mechanics deposit was located.

sources.title: What Differences Exist Between the Lead and Trail Wrist in Extensor Carpi Ulnaris Activity and Golf Swing Joint Kinematics in Sub-Elite Golfers?
sources.correction_check_method: Publisher, PubMed, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Sub-elite golfers sampled for lead-trail wrist comparison; the source population does not represent all skill, age, sex, handedness, or impairment groups.
sources.apparatus: Bilateral extensor carpi ulnaris surface EMG with golf-swing joint kinematics.
sources.estimand: Lead-trail differences in one sampled forearm muscle activation and associated joint kinematics.
sources.uncertainty: Electrode, normalization, detector, cross-talk, kinematic-model, and participant variation remain distinct and are not a hand-wrench uncertainty model.
limitations: One superficial muscle cannot identify wrist torque, co-contraction, or bilateral grip allocation.
Observational lead-trail differences do not identify causal preparation, braking, or preload strategy.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed synchronized EMG, wrench, and motion deposit was located.

sources.title: A Biomechanical Model of the Scapulothoracic Joint to Accurately Capture Scapular Kinematics During Shoulder Movements
sources.correction_check_method: Original PLOS record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Previously collected non-golf shoulder-task bone-pin kinematics used to evaluate a customizable scapulothoracic model.
sources.apparatus: Four-degree-of-freedom scapulothoracic mobilizer evaluated against registered bone-pin marker kinematics for three shoulder tasks.
sources.estimand: Scapular marker reconstruction and model-noise behavior, including reported approximately two-millimetre RMS accuracy in the tested tasks.
sources.uncertainty: Task, morphology, bone-pin reference, marker noise, model constraint, and transport-to-golf uncertainty remain separate.
limitations: The source validates a shoulder-model formulation in non-golf tasks, not golf scapular dynamics or muscle control.
Good marker reconstruction does not identify scapulothoracic reaction loads, muscle forces, or bilateral hand allocation.
sources.raw_data_status: The source reports an open model and analysis resources, but no governed golf participant dataset.

sources.title: Contribution of Muscle Short-Range Stiffness to Initial Changes in Joint Kinetics and Kinematics During Perturbations to Standing Balance
sources.correction_check_method: Original PMC record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Non-golf standing-balance perturbation data and simulation context.
sources.apparatus: Musculoskeletal simulation used to isolate short-range muscle-stiffness contributions to early perturbation response.
sources.estimand: Model-dependent contribution of short-range stiffness to initial joint kinetics and kinematics.
sources.uncertainty: Muscle parameters, activation history, posture, perturbation, model structure, and transport to rapid golf motion are not interchangeable.
limitations: The result is model- and standing-task-dependent rather than direct golf tissue measurement.
It does not identify wrist, scapular, or hand-wrench stiffness during a swing.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed golf activation, tissue, and bilateral-wrench dataset is supplied.

sources.title: Effect of Series Elasticity on Delay in Development of Tension Relative to Stiffness During Muscle Activation
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Non-golf experimental muscle preparation; it is not a participant golf study.
sources.apparatus: Experimental activation and series-elastic manipulation used to compare tension and stiffness development timing.
sources.estimand: Delay between activation-related stiffness and transmitted tension under the source preparation.
sources.uncertainty: Preparation, activation, compliance, force, stiffness, and scale do not directly transport to an intact swinging arm.
limitations: The preparation and task are not golf and cannot establish human wrist preload or slack.
Tension and stiffness timing does not identify net joint moment or endpoint wrench allocation.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed intact-human golf dataset is associated with this mechanistic source.

sources.title: Effects of Series Elastic Compliance on Muscle Force Summation and the Rate of Force Rise
sources.correction_check_method: Publisher, PubMed, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Non-golf experimental muscle-tendon preparation rather than an intact golfer sample.
sources.apparatus: Controlled series-elastic compliance with force-rise measurements under the source protocol.
sources.estimand: Compliance-dependent force summation and rate of force rise.
sources.uncertainty: Preparation, compliance, excitation, force calibration, and intact-system transport are outside the present golf dataset.
limitations: The source motivates a compliance mechanism but does not measure golf muscle-tendon dynamics.
Force-rise effects do not establish a beneficial preparation, slack, or timing strategy.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed intact-human golf dataset is associated with this mechanistic source.

sources.title: Within- and Between-Session Reliability of Golf Swing Variables Using the TrackMan Launch Monitor in Talented Golfers
sources.correction_check_method: Publisher, PubMed, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Talented golfers observed within and between sessions; the sample is not a universal device-validation population.
sources.apparatus: TrackMan launch monitor under the source's repeated-session golf protocol.
sources.estimand: Within- and between-session reliability of selected device-reported golf-swing variables.
sources.uncertainty: Reliability, reference-device validity, alignment, firmware, environment, impact location, and shot matching are distinct.
limitations: Reliability in one protocol does not establish accuracy for every metric, firmware, setup, club, or population.
Launch-monitor outcomes do not identify internal energy-transfer or control mechanisms.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed shot-level deposit linked to the required synchronized project modalities was located.

sources.title: Effects of the Golfer--Ground Interaction on Clubhead Speed in Skilled Male Golfers
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed, publisher, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Sixty-three highly skilled male golfers with handicaps no greater than three.
sources.apparatus: Golf-swing kinematics and golfer-ground force and moment measurements under the source protocol.
sources.estimand: Associations between selected golfer-ground parameters and maximum clubhead speed.
sources.uncertainty: Observational association, variable selection, participant, coordinate, filtering, equipment, and unmeasured-confounding uncertainty remain.
limitations: The all-male skilled sample and observational design do not identify a causal ground-transfer strategy.
Ground wrench does not uniquely identify bilateral hand, joint, or muscle allocation.
sources.raw_data_status: No qualifying governed participant-level source package was admitted to the project.

sources.title: A Three Dimensional Kinematic and Kinetic Study of the Golf Swing
sources.correction_check_method: Original journal and PubMed metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Eighty-four male and one female amateur golfers spanning skill levels, with detailed comparisons of four subjects.
sources.apparatus: Multi-camera motion analysis driving a variable full-body golfer model coupled to a flexible club model.
sources.estimand: Model-derived golfer and club kinematics, kinetics, interaction loads, work, power, and deformation with population variation.
sources.uncertainty: Motion reconstruction, inertial parameters, flexible-club model, inverse dynamics, participant imbalance, and selected-subject reporting remain model dependent.
limitations: Most mechanical outputs are model-derived rather than directly measured interface or muscle quantities.
One female participant and heterogeneous amateurs do not support sex-specific or population-wide inference.
sources.raw_data_status: The project has no governed participant-level trajectories and model inputs from this study.

sources.title: How Well Does Club Head Speed Correlate With Golf Handicaps?
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Forty-five male golfers aged 18 to 80 years with handicaps from two to twenty-seven.
sources.apparatus: Clubhead-speed and handicap assessment under the source's observational protocol.
sources.estimand: Sample association between clubhead speed and handicap.
sources.uncertainty: Sample selection, age, equipment, repeated-shot, device, handicap, and confounding uncertainty do not identify mechanism.
limitations: The all-male sample and bivariate association do not identify age, skill, or causal transfer effects.
Handicap and speed do not measure internal work, momentum redistribution, or bilateral control.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed participant-level deposit was located.

sources.title: Movement Variability in the Golf Swing
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed, publisher, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Golf movement-variability literature rather than one governed participant cohort.
sources.apparatus: Synthesis of golf-swing variability concepts, measurements, and tasks across source studies.
sources.estimand: Within- and between-player movement variability and its task-dependent interpretation.
sources.uncertainty: Study designs, signals, event normalization, skill definitions, equipment, and variability metrics are heterogeneous.
limitations: A synthesis of variability does not provide a project-ready participant distribution or measurement covariance.
Variability can reflect adaptation, noise, or task redundancy and is not inherently beneficial or adverse.
sources.raw_data_status: Source-level participant data remain distributed across the reviewed literature.

sources.title: The Biomechanics of the Modern Golf Swing: Implications for Lower Back Injuries
sources.correction_check_method: Publisher and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Lower-back injury and modern golf-swing biomechanics literature rather than one prospective cohort.
sources.apparatus: Review of swing biomechanics, spinal loading concepts, and injury implications across heterogeneous studies.
sources.estimand: Contextual relationship between modern swing mechanics, spinal loading, and lower-back injury hypotheses.
sources.uncertainty: Exposure, injury definition, tissue load, individual capacity, study design, and causal attribution vary across sources.
limitations: Review context cannot convert project mechanical proxies into individual tissue load or injury risk.
Performance and injury objectives require separate outcomes, uncertainty, and governance.
sources.raw_data_status: No prospective injury-linked project dataset is present.

sources.title: Golf Swing Biomechanics: A Systematic Review and Methodological Recommendations for Kinematics
sources.correction_check_method: Original PMC record and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Golf kinematics literature with heterogeneous populations, clubs, tasks, and protocols.
sources.apparatus: Systematic review of motion-capture, segment-definition, event, and processing methods used in golf biomechanics.
sources.estimand: Methodological comparability and recommended reporting for golf-swing kinematics.
sources.uncertainty: Marker sets, coordinate conventions, filtering, events, tasks, clubs, and populations vary across included studies.
limitations: Methodological recommendations do not supply participant-level trajectories or bilateral mechanics.
Kinematics alone cannot identify energy flow, muscle action, or individual hand allocation.
sources.raw_data_status: The review does not provide one governed, synchronized multimodal participant deposit.

sources.title: Effects of Fatigue on Golf Performance
sources.correction_check_method: PubMed, publisher, and Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24.
sources.population: Golfers exposed to the source's golf-specific fatiguing protocol.
sources.apparatus: Pre-post body-position, weight-transfer, pelvis and trunk rotation, clubhead-speed, and shot-consistency assessment.
sources.estimand: Association of the registered fatigue protocol with swing mechanics, speed, and consistency changes.
sources.uncertainty: Fatigue induction, physiological state, repeated shots, learning, device, participant, and model-selection uncertainty remain.
limitations: One fatigue protocol does not reproduce all round, practice, local-muscle, cognitive, or injury-related fatigue states.
Pre-post associations do not identify the internal transfer mechanism or prescribe a robust strategy.
sources.raw_data_status: No governed synchronized fatigue, bilateral-wrench, EMG, shaft, and launch deposit was located.

sources.title: Muscle Patterns Underlying Voluntary Modulation of Co-Contraction
sources.correction_check_method: Original PLOS and PMC records plus Crossref relation metadata reviewed on 2026-08-24; this check corrected a previously mismatched bibliography DOI and author list.
sources.population: Human participants performing multidirectional isometric hand-force and voluntary co-contraction tasks outside golf.
sources.apparatus: Endpoint force measurement, seventeen-muscle surface EMG, virtual targets, and simulated disturbances with null-space analysis.
sources.estimand: Muscle-activation components that change co-contraction without changing the estimated endpoint force mapping.
sources.uncertainty: EMG-to-force regression, null-space estimation, electrode signals, isometric-task transport, and virtual rather than physical perturbation remain.
limitations: The source demonstrates redundant co-contraction patterns in an isometric non-golf task, not a swing strategy.
EMG null-space components do not directly measure endpoint stiffness, wrist torque, or bilateral grip wrench.
sources.raw_data_status: The open article provides methodological evidence but not a governed golf participant dataset.

coverage.current_answer: Pelvis pose and velocity are measurable under declared methods, and selected sampled associations and fatigue responses exist; neither peak order nor pelvis motion alone identifies transfer.
limitations: Coordinate, marker, filter, event, population, club, and task definitions vary.
Pelvis kinematics do not identify ground, joint, muscle, or hand-wrench causality.
coverage.data_gate: Governed participant-held-out synchronized motion and external-wrench data with method sensitivity are required for project mechanism tests.

coverage.current_answer: Thorax kinematics and selected fatigue or performance associations are measurable, but anatomical torso control and causal energy transfer remain unresolved.
limitations: Thorax definitions, marker sets, X-factor methods, and event timing are not invariant.
The reduced model's proximal coordinate is not an anatomical thorax state.
coverage.data_gate: Use a declared thorax frame, synchronized bilateral mechanics, participant holdout, and adverse coordinate-method controls.

coverage.current_answer: Golf scapular EMG and a non-golf scapulothoracic model motivate explicit scapular states, but neither identifies golf scapular mechanics or wrench allocation.
limitations: Surface EMG is not scapular kinematics, force, or torque.
Bone-pin model evaluation used non-golf shoulder tasks.
coverage.data_gate: Acquire validated dynamic scapular tracking with synchronized EMG and bilateral mechanics; preserve soft-tissue and model constraint uncertainty.

coverage.current_answer: Upper-limb inverse dynamics and a shoulder-model formulation provide bounded methods, while golf glenohumeral load and muscle allocation remain model dependent.
limitations: Ball-joint and scapulothoracic assumptions affect inferred loads.
Closed-chain mechanics require independent contact information.
coverage.data_gate: Qualify subject-scaled shoulder geometry and residuals against synchronized golf motion and bilateral external loads.

coverage.current_answer: Golf elbow kinematics and inverse-dynamics loads can be estimated when the internal grip wrench is measured, but muscle and task allocation remain unresolved.
limitations: One study used a custom grip and model-dependent inward inverse dynamics.
Net elbow load does not identify individual muscle work.
coverage.data_gate: Replicate with independent calibrated bilateral mechanics, subject scaling, participant holdout, and model sensitivity.

coverage.current_answer: Forearm motion, inverse-dynamics load, and selected surface activation are observable, while pronation-supination control and muscle force remain unqualified.
limitations: One-muscle EMG and net joint loads are distinct estimands.
The project articulated model does not yet include calibrated forearm muscle dynamics.
coverage.data_gate: Use a declared forearm frame, sufficient marker or imaging observability, synchronized activation, and independent loads.

coverage.current_answer: Wrist kinematics, selected muscle activation, and model-dependent net load have human precedent; active versus passive torque and lead-trail allocation remain unidentified.
limitations: Net moment, direct hand moment, force-generated couple, and muscle force are not interchangeable.
Surface activation does not identify passive tissue or co-contraction.
coverage.data_gate: Acquire synchronized bilateral wrenches, motion, multi-muscle activation, and uncertainty-qualified tissue observables.

coverage.current_answer: Hand segment motion and a measured internal grip wrench have precedent, but distributed contact and each external hand wrench are not directly recovered.
limitations: The custom split grip perturbs geometry and measures one internal section wrench.
Lumped hand joints omit pressure distribution and moving contact centers.
coverage.data_gate: Qualify a two-hand instrumented grip with contact-center tracking, cross-talk correction, normal-club controls, and participant holdout.

coverage.current_answer: Opposing hand actions and an internal six-axis wrench have been observed, but no located governed dataset supplies synchronized independent bilateral external six-axis hand wrenches.
limitations: One internal wrench is not two complete external hand wrenches.
Net club motion retains allocation null modes.
coverage.data_gate: Physical device qualification and governed participant-held-out acquisition remain externally blocked.

coverage.current_answer: Golf ground wrenches and selected speed associations are measurable, while causal transfer, biological control, and club-energy attribution require additional synchronized mechanics.
limitations: Association does not establish direction of causality.
Force or impulse alone is not contact power or internal energy transfer.
coverage.data_gate: Require participant-separated calibration, Newton-Euler closure, frame transport, uncertainty, negative controls, and held-out testing.

coverage.current_answer: Independent sources establish plausible stiffness, compliance, activation-history, and co-contraction mechanisms outside golf; their magnitude and role in a swing are unmeasured.
limitations: Preparations and tasks differ materially from a golf swing.
Muscle redundancy and constitutive uncertainty prevent force identification from motion and EMG alone.
coverage.data_gate: Synchronized EMG, ultrasound or qualified tissue proxy, bilateral mechanics, calibrated activation dynamics, and participant holdout are required.

coverage.current_answer: A golf-specific fatigue protocol has been associated with changes in mechanics, speed, and consistency, but robustness of the proposed transfer mechanisms under fatigue is untested.
limitations: Fatigue state depends on protocol, localization, recovery, skill, and measurement.
A pre-post study does not identify the internal mechanism of change.
coverage.data_gate: Freeze fatigue and recovery states, retain order and learning controls, and test mechanism parameters and residuals on held-out participants.

coverage.current_answer: Golf biomechanics literature motivates separate spinal-load and injury questions, but the project has no calibrated tissue-load or prospective injury outcome.
limitations: Mechanical proxies cannot be relabeled as tissue injury risk.
Individual capacity, exposure, symptoms, impairment, and clinical history are absent.
coverage.data_gate: A separately approved prospective safety protocol is required; performance optimization cannot substitute for injury qualification.

coverage.current_answer: Large between-golfer variation and bounded age, skill, and speed associations are documented, but the project lacks a representative multimodal population distribution.
limitations: Samples are often male, right-handed, selected by skill, and equipment specific.
Population association does not establish within-person intervention response.
coverage.data_gate: Recruit to stated target populations, preserve participant separation, and report subgroup uncertainty without unsupported pooling.

coverage.current_answer: Instrumented-grip perturbation and launch-monitor reliability have bounded precedents, while shaft, grip, club, device, and firmware transport are unqualified for the proposed mechanisms.
limitations: Instrumented equipment can alter mass, inertia, feel, contact, and motion.
Reliability does not establish device accuracy or mechanism validity.
coverage.data_gate: Use calibrated equipment strata, randomized or counterbalanced controls, matched impact, and held-out device and club evaluation.

coverage.current_answer: Golf motion and variability depend on club, intent, target, shot type, and analysis method; no one task defines a universal optimal transfer strategy.
limitations: Speed, carry, accuracy, load, robustness, and partial-shot objectives are not equivalent.
Event and coordinate methods can change the apparent sequence.
coverage.data_gate: Preregister task families and acceptable-shot criteria, then evaluate mechanism and strategy claims separately on held-out tasks.
